chapters.title: ICT-Related Incident Management, Classification and Reporting

articles.title: Subject matter
articles.requirement: Establishes uniform requirements for ICT risk management, incident reporting, resilience testing, and third-party risk for financial entities

articles.title: Scope
articles.requirement: Defines which financial entities are in scope: credit institutions, payment institutions, investment firms, insurance, CASPs, CCPs, CSDs, etc.

articles.title: Definitions
articles.requirement: Defines key terms: ICT risk, ICT-related incident, major ICT-related incident, cyber threat, critical ICT third-party service provider, etc.

articles.title: Proportionality principle
articles.requirement: Apply DORA requirements proportionate to size, nature, scale, and complexity of activities; microenterprises have lighter obligations

articles.title: Governance and organisation
articles.requirement: Management body defines and approves ICT risk management strategy; is ultimately responsible for ICT risk; allocates adequate resources

articles.title: ICT risk management framework
articles.requirement: Documented ICT risk management framework; reviewed at least annually; approved by management body; includes strategies, policies, procedures

articles.title: ICT systems, protocols and tools
articles.requirement: Adequate, resilient ICT systems; capacity planning; network segmentation; encryption standards; kept up to date

articles.title: Identification
articles.requirement: Identify all ICT-supported business functions and assets; classify by criticality; maintain up-to-date inventory; document dependencies and interconnections

articles.title: Protection and prevention
articles.requirement: ICT security policies; access controls; change management; patch management; endpoint protection; data integrity mechanisms

articles.title: Detection
articles.requirement: Anomaly detection mechanisms; monitoring of ICT operations and infrastructure; multiple layers of control; alert thresholds

articles.title: Response and recovery
articles.requirement: ICT business continuity policy; response and recovery plans; estimated recovery times; communication procedures during ICT disruptions

articles.title: Backup policies and procedures, restoration and recovery procedures and methods
articles.requirement: Backup policies specifying scope, frequency, methods; recovery procedures; regular testing of backup and restoration; geographic separation of backup sites

articles.title: Learning and evolving
articles.requirement: Post-incident analysis; update ICT risk management framework based on lessons learned; threat intelligence integration; security awareness training

articles.title: Communication
articles.requirement: ICT crisis communication plans; internal escalation procedures; external stakeholder and public communication; responsible vulnerability disclosure

articles.title: Further harmonisation of ICT risk management tools, methods, processes and policies
articles.requirement: ESAs develop RTS to further specify ICT risk management framework elements including tools, methods, processes, and policies

articles.title: Simplified ICT risk management framework
articles.requirement: Simplified framework for entities meeting criteria (small, non-interconnected); must still cover core ICT risk management elements proportionately

articles.title: ICT-related incident management process
articles.requirement: Establish ICT-related incident management process to detect, manage, and notify ICT-related incidents; assign roles and responsibilities; classify incidents

articles.title: Classification of ICT-related incidents and cyber threats
articles.requirement: Classification criteria for incidents and cyber threats: number of clients affected, duration, geographic spread, data losses, criticality of services affected, economic impact

articles.title: Reporting of major ICT-related incidents and voluntary notification of significant cyber threats
articles.requirement: Report major incidents to competent authority: initial notification (4h), intermediate report (72h), final report (1 month); voluntary notification of significant cyber threats

articles.title: Harmonisation of reporting content and templates
articles.requirement: ESAs develop RTS specifying content, timelines, and templates for incident reports; common taxonomy; single reporting hub

articles.title: Centralisation of reporting of major ICT-related incidents
articles.requirement: Feasibility of establishing single EU hub for major ICT incident reporting; ESAs assess and report to Commission

articles.title: Supervisory feedback
articles.requirement: Competent authorities provide feedback on incident reports; guidance on handling; anonymised information on similar incidents sector-wide

articles.title: Operational or security payment-related incidents concerning credit institutions, payment institutions, account information service providers, and electronic money institutions
articles.requirement: Specific provisions for payment-related incidents: reporting aligned with PSD2/EMD2 requirements; competent authority forwards to relevant ESA

articles.title: General requirements for the performance of digital operational resilience testing
articles.requirement: Establish comprehensive digital operational resilience testing programme; proportionate to size and risk profile; reviewed annually by management body

articles.title: Testing of ICT tools and systems
articles.requirement: Testing includes vulnerability assessments, network security assessments, gap analyses, physical security reviews, software source code reviews, scenario-based testing, compatibility testing

articles.title: Advanced testing of ICT tools, systems and processes based on TLPT
articles.requirement: Threat-led penetration testing at least every 3 years for significant entities; cover critical functions and live production systems; external testers; results reported to competent authority

articles.title: Requirements for testers for the carrying out of TLPT
articles.requirement: TLPT testers must meet specific requirements: highest professional suitability, technical capability, independence, accreditation; internal testers permitted with conditions

articles.title: General principles
articles.section: Key principles for ICT third-party risk management
articles.requirement: Policy for ICT third-party risk management; risk-based approach; pre-contractual due diligence; register of all ICT third-party arrangements; ultimate responsibility remains with financial entity

articles.title: Preliminary assessment of ICT concentration risk at entity level
articles.section: Key principles for ICT third-party risk management
articles.requirement: Assess ICT concentration risk before entering arrangements; consider substitutability, number of critical providers, geographic concentration; report to competent authority

articles.title: Key contractual provisions
articles.section: Key principles for ICT third-party risk management
articles.requirement: Mandatory contractual elements: SLAs, audit rights, exit provisions, data location, subcontracting controls, security measures, incident support, cooperation with authorities

articles.title: Designation of critical ICT third-party service providers
articles.section: Oversight framework of critical ICT third-party service providers
articles.requirement: ESAs designate critical ICT third-party service providers based on systemic importance, substitutability, and number of financial entities relying on them

articles.title: Structure of the Oversight Framework
articles.section: Oversight framework of critical ICT third-party service providers
articles.requirement: Lead Overseer (EBA, ESMA, or EIOPA) appointed per critical provider; joint examination team; oversight access rights and procedures

articles.title: Tasks of the Lead Overseer
articles.section: Oversight framework of critical ICT third-party service providers
articles.requirement: Lead Overseer assesses critical provider's ICT risk management, security, and operational resilience; monitors compliance; issues recommendations

articles.title: Operational coordination between Lead Overseers
articles.section: Oversight framework of critical ICT third-party service providers
articles.requirement: Lead Overseers coordinate activities to ensure consistent oversight approach across critical providers; share findings and best practices

articles.title: Powers of the Lead Overseer
articles.section: Oversight framework of critical ICT third-party service providers
articles.requirement: Request information and documents; conduct general investigations; conduct on-site inspections; issue recommendations; impose follow-up measures

articles.title: Exercise of the powers of the Lead Overseer outside the Union
articles.section: Oversight framework of critical ICT third-party service providers
articles.requirement: Where critical provider is established outside EU, Lead Overseer may establish subsidiary oversight office in EU or exercise powers through cooperation arrangements

articles.title: Request for information
articles.section: Oversight framework of critical ICT third-party service providers
articles.requirement: Lead Overseer may request any information needed to carry out oversight duties; critical provider must respond within specified timeframe

articles.title: General investigations
articles.section: Oversight framework of critical ICT third-party service providers
articles.requirement: Lead Overseer may conduct general investigations including examination of records, documents, systems, and oral explanations from staff

articles.title: Inspections
articles.section: Oversight framework of critical ICT third-party service providers
articles.requirement: Lead Overseer may conduct on-site inspections at any premises of the critical provider with advance notification; access to systems and data

articles.title: Ongoing oversight
articles.section: Oversight framework of critical ICT third-party service providers
articles.requirement: Lead Overseer conducts ongoing monitoring of critical providers' compliance with recommendations; follow-up on remediation plans; escalation procedures

articles.title: Harmonisation of conditions enabling the conduct of the oversight activities
articles.section: Oversight framework of critical ICT third-party service providers
articles.requirement: ESAs develop RTS harmonising conditions for oversight activities to ensure consistent approach across Lead Overseers

articles.title: Follow-up by competent authorities
articles.section: Oversight framework of critical ICT third-party service providers
articles.requirement: Competent authorities of financial entities follow up on recommendations issued by Lead Overseer to critical providers; may require entities to adjust arrangements

articles.title: Oversight fees
articles.section: Oversight framework of critical ICT third-party service providers
articles.requirement: Annual oversight fees charged to designated critical ICT third-party service providers; calculated based on turnover and number of financial entity clients

articles.title: International cooperation
articles.section: Oversight framework of critical ICT third-party service providers
articles.requirement: ESAs cooperate with third-country authorities on oversight of critical ICT providers with international operations; information exchange arrangements

articles.title: Information-sharing arrangements on cyber threat information and intelligence
articles.requirement: Financial entities may exchange cyber threat information within trusted communities; legal framework; confidentiality protections; anonymisation; voluntary basis

articles.title: Competent authorities
articles.requirement: Member States designate competent authorities for DORA supervision; powers of investigation, enforcement, and sanction

articles.title: Cooperation with structures and authorities established by Directive (EU) 2022/2555
articles.requirement: DORA competent authorities cooperate with NIS2 Directive authorities; information sharing on cross-sector ICT risks and incidents

articles.title: Cooperation between authorities
articles.requirement: Competent authorities cooperate with each other and with ESAs; exchange information; coordinate supervision of cross-border entities

articles.title: Financial cross-sector exercises, communication and cooperation
articles.requirement: ESAs may organise cross-sector resilience exercises; promote communication between financial entities and authorities during crises

articles.title: Administrative penalties and remedial measures
articles.requirement: Member States provide for effective, proportionate, and dissuasive administrative penalties for DORA breaches; minimum powers for competent authorities

articles.title: Exercise of the power to impose administrative penalties and remedial measures
articles.requirement: Rules on exercising penalty powers: aggravating and mitigating factors, proportionality assessment, right of defence, procedural requirements

articles.title: Criminal penalties
articles.requirement: Member States may provide for criminal penalties for DORA breaches; must notify Commission; penalties must be effective, proportionate, and dissuasive

articles.title: Notification duties
articles.requirement: Member States notify Commission and ESAs of laws and regulations transposing DORA penalty provisions

articles.title: Publication of administrative penalties
articles.requirement: Competent authorities publish enforcement decisions on their websites; anonymisation rules for natural persons; 5-year retention minimum

articles.title: Professional secrecy
articles.requirement: All persons involved in DORA supervision and oversight bound by professional secrecy obligations; conditions for sharing confidential information

articles.title: Data protection
articles.requirement: Processing of personal data under DORA must comply with GDPR and relevant data protection rules; limited to purposes necessary for DORA compliance

articles.title: Exercise of the delegation
articles.requirement: Conditions for Commission delegated acts under DORA; delegation period; Parliament and Council revocation rights; scrutiny procedure

articles.title: Review clause
articles.requirement: Commission reviews DORA application by 17 January 2028; considers effectiveness, new technologies, evolving risks; may propose amendments

articles.title: Amendments to Regulation (EC) No 1060/2009
articles.section: Amendments
articles.requirement: Technical amendments to Credit Rating Agencies Regulation to align with DORA ICT risk management requirements

articles.title: Amendments to Regulation (EU) No 648/2012
articles.section: Amendments
articles.requirement: Amendments to EMIR (European Market Infrastructure Regulation) to align with DORA

articles.title: Amendments to Regulation (EU) No 909/2014
articles.section: Amendments
articles.requirement: Amendments to CSDR (Central Securities Depositories Regulation) to align with DORA

articles.title: Amendments to Regulation (EU) No 600/2014
articles.section: Amendments
articles.requirement: Amendments to MiFIR (Markets in Financial Instruments Regulation) to align with DORA

articles.title: Amendment to Regulation (EU) 2016/1011
articles.section: Amendments
articles.requirement: Amendment to Benchmarks Regulation to align with DORA

articles.title: Entry into force and application
articles.requirement: Entered into force 16 January 2023; applies from 17 January 2025
